title: Address rate-limit hysteresis causing aggregated sparklines underreport
creator: Marco Diaz
description:
Summary: Some Console aggregated sparklines (per-tenant and per-model) are underreporting peak token consumption during and immediately after sustained rate-limit events. This manifests as flattened peaks and lower peak-to-baseline ratios on 1h/6h sparklines even though raw request/usage ledgers show normal counts once retries are accounted for.

Observed behavior: When a tenant hits a token-based rate limit, the ingestion pipeline emits a series of rate-limit 'hold' events and later a cluster of retry/resume events. Our aggregation layer applies a hysteresis window to avoid double-counting retries, but the current hysteresis logic collapses legitimate resumed tokens into the hold window when the resume timestamp falls within the same aggregation bucket, effectively discarding those tokens from the per-model sparklines while the ledger shows them. This mainly affects streaming-prefix-heavy workloads and bursty retry patterns (e.g., SDKs with immediate retry backoff jitter).

Scope: Reproducible on staging with synthetic tenant-replays and observed in production on ~7% of tenants during last month's incident window (see incident dash). Affects console sparklines (1m/1h/6h zooms) and derived per-model peak metrics used for cost optimization suggestions. Does not affect billing ledger totals (billing pipeline eventually reconciles); affects client-visible charts and alerts.

Root cause hypothesis: The hysteresis/merge step in the streaming aggregator tags "hold" windows and merges adjacent resume tokens if their event_time delta < hysteresis_ms. The hysteresis threshold was tuned conservatively for deduplication of immediate-retry spam, but because rate-limit hold windows can span multiple aggregation buckets and retries are delayed by client backoff, resumed tokens are incorrectly merged only on the aggregation window boundary. The result is dropped tokens in the aggregator's per-model counters used for sparklines.

Plan: 1) Add an event-level ingress tag that preserves resume vs original timestamps and preserves provenance for tokens that were rate-limited then resumed; 2) Modify hysteresis to be bucket-aware: only dedupe tokens that both (a) share identical provenance fingerprint and (b) fall within a short absolute dedupe window (e.g., 250ms) regardless of bucket boundaries; 3) Implement a fast path to rehydrate merged tokens during backfill/replay runs so late reconstructions restore per-model sparklines; 4) Add a correctness e2e test in the synthetic-replay harness and a dashboard-based smoke test for affected tenants; 5) Roll out change behind a feature flag and A/B compare console sparklines vs control for 72h.

Acceptance criteria: - Sparklines on staging replay match raw ledger-derived per-model 95th percentile peak within 3% for synthetic burst tests. - No increase in duplicate invoiceable tokens in billing reports. - Feature flagged rollout shows improved peak preservation on A-group vs control in 72h run.

Notes: This ticket is focused on chart correctness and does not change billing semantics. Any change that risks altering finalized billing totals must be done in close coordination with Billing team and recorded in a separate billing reconciliation RFC.
